description:
crate-jmap-base-client/benches/session_and_urls.rs:111-129 builds the large-session JSON fixture by calling `accounts.push_str(&format!(...))` inside a `for i in 0..num_accounts` loop. This is the `clippy::format_push_string` anti-pattern: every iteration allocates a fresh `String` for the format! macro and immediately drops it after the push_str copy.

Idiomatic Rust uses `std::fmt::Write` on the destination string directly: `use std::fmt::Write as _; write!(accounts, r#""A{i:03}": ..."#).unwrap();`. `write!` formats straight into the existing buffer with no intermediate allocation. For a 100-account fixture this saves 100 short-lived heap allocations per bench iteration.

What goes wrong: the benches measure deserialize cost, but the fixture builder itself runs in setup, not in the timed section, so this does not corrupt bench numbers. The engineering basis is clippy hygiene + consistency with the workspace's hot-path performance discipline (cf. commit 2959118 'return Cow from percent_encode to skip allocation' and e04d589 'drop Value clones in 4 client capability deserialize sites'). A bench harness in a crate that takes per-allocation perf seriously should not itself model the anti-pattern.

Low priority — bench setup, not production code. Fix is mechanical.
title: benches/session_and_urls.rs uses String::push_str(&format!()) in a loop — format-push-string anti-idiom
